title: LChS Documentation - Overview
content: Land CHaracterization System Overview Since 1996, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has been developing international guidance and standards for land cover and land use monitoring. Building on the foundation of Land Cover Classification System (LCCS) and the Land Cover MetaLanguage (LCML) – ISO 19144-2, FAO developed Land CHaracterization System (LChS) software. LChS is a standalone, open-source and web-based application that provides a user-friendly graphical interface characterizing and representing land cover and land use through a modelling approach. It represents land cover and land use considering the structure and relationships of the classes, patterns, elements, properties and characteristics. It has been developed to aim at characterizing land cover and land use, meaning that its future development will also consider the standards ISO 19144-3 on land use and 19144-4 on registration and implementation (under development). The LCHS is also accompanied by two sematic interoperability assessment tools: Similarity Assessment – compares legends across domains. Legend Connector – enables assignment between classification systems.

title: LChS Documentation - Examples
content: Examples I. Mangroves Class Name: Mangroves Class Code: MNG Class Description: The mangroves are defined by two distinct strata. The first stratum is woody growth forms with a vegetation cover ranging from 40 to 100 percent. Vegetation height varies between 1 and 20 meters, and the leaf phenological characteristic is evergreen. The floristic aspect of the mangroves comprises of species Rhizophora sp. The second stratum is water, with the coverage ranging from 0 to 100 percent. The water salinity is defined as brackish, and the artificiality is natural. title: LChS Documentation - User Interface
content: User Interface Figure: User Interface Main Toolbar The main toolbar contains three dropdown menus. Figure: Main Toolbar The menu includes: ‘File’: Using this menu a user can create new, import, export and delete a legend. As well as manage saved work and user defined characteristics. Figure: File Menu ‘Wizards’: This option enables users to build the legend through a guided and user-friendly interface as well as managing any user-defined characteristics. Figure: Wizards Menu ‘Resources’: This menu provides all the relevant resources related to LChS software as well as other tools and documentation. Figure: Resources Menu Shortcut Toolbar The shortcut toolbar contains shortcuts to the new (create new legend), import (imports legend), export (exports legend), save (save work progress), validate (validates the created legend), legend wizard (create legends in guided way), uses definitions (manage saved work and defined characteristics), docs (access to online documentation), and guided tour (guide to explain each panel in the software) options. Figure: Shortcut Toolbar. Quick actions - new, import, export, save, validate, user definitions, legend wizard, docs & guided tour Elements Panel The elements panel contains a set of independent elements whose combination, according to the LCML rules, will form a land cover class. The elements composing the class are related to the physiognomic and/or structural characterization of the land cover object. Two main elements are present: 1. vegetation (biotic) elements and 2. non-vegetated (abiotic) elements. A user can easily add them into the land cover class by double-clicking, as well as a user can search by typing the name of the element using search bar. Figure: Elements Panel Vegetation (biotic) Woody TreesShrubs Herbaceous ForbsGraminoids Lichens & Mosses Algae Non-vegetated (abiotic) Abiotic surfaces ArtificialBuilt-upLinear surface Natural surfaces Soils & sand deposits Water bodies & associated surfaces Legend Panel The legend panel lists all the land cover classes in the legend being worked on. A user can also search the land cover class by using search tab in the legend panel. Figure: Legend Panel Legend editing and graphic overview pane The legend editing and graphic overview panel allows users to view and modify legends by simply clicking on the corresponding boxes. Below Figure shows an example of a legend, graphical overview of the legend and its classes and user can export the UML diagram as an image in PNG format by clicking on the export diagram button. Figure: Legend editing and graphic overview pane Element properties panel The legend editing and graphic overview panel is linked with the element properties panel, since properties are a further specialization of the elements with regards to their physiognomic or structural aspect. From the element properties panel, the user can determine the properties of the element after it has been added to the legend tree. Figure: Element Properties Panel Element characteristics panel The legend editing and graphic overview panel is linked with the element characteristics panel, since characteristics are a further specialization e.g. climate, floristic aspects, water stress etc. From the element characteristics panel, the user can determine characteristics on addition to the legend tree. The user selects a characteristic group and fills the specific characteristic values in this panel. Figure: Element Characteristics Panel Notifications panel The notifications panel lists all the LCHS generated notifications including errors whenever a saving function is undertaken. Figure: Notification Panel

title: LChS Documentation - Workflows
content: Land Cover Legend Creation Workflows I. New Legend From the menu toolbar select 'File' then 'New' [Select 'New' from the shortcut toolbar]. Select 'Yes' to confirm legend clearing. Select 'No' not to restore auto-save. In the legend pane, select 'Legend' and enter the legend's name, description and author in the properties panel. Select 'Save Properties' to save the legend's properties. In the legend pane, select 'Class 1' and enter the class' name, description, code and colour in the properties panel. Select 'Save Properties' to save the class' properties. In the properties panel, select 'Add Horizontal Pattern' to add a horizontal pattern to the class. In the legend pane, select 'Horizontal Pattern 1' and enter the horizontal pattern's description, cover, occurrence and pattern type in the properties panel. Select 'Save Properties' to save the horizontal pattern's properties. In the properties panel, select 'Add Stratum' to add a stratum to the horizontal pattern. In the legend pane, select 'Stratum 1' and enter the stratum's description, presence type, portioning, and On Top details in the properties panel. While the stratum is highlighted in the legend pane, double click on all the elements in the element panel that are relevant to the stratum to add them. In the legend pane, select an element and enter its properties in the properties panel. Select 'Save Properties' to save the elements' properties. While the element is highlighted in the legend pane, select a characteristic group in the characteristics panel. Enter the element's characteristics in the characteristics sheet that appears above the characteristic groups. Select 'Save Characteristics' to save the elements' characteristics. From the shortcut toolbar select 'Validate' to check for any errors in the legend From the menu toolbar select 'File' then 'Export' to export the legend [Select 'Export' from the shortcut toolbar] / [Select 'Export diagram' from the legend pane] Your browser does not support the video tag. Video: Creating a new legend II. Import Legend Importing a legend file. From the menu toolbar select 'File' then 'Import' [Select 'Import' from the shortcut toolbar]. In the new 'Import Characterization Legend' window under 'Select Legend Source', select 'Legend File'. Click on the blue 'Select Legend' button and navigate and select the legend file to import [Drag and drop the legend file you wish to import into the 'Drag and Drop Legend File Here' area]. Note: LChS can process .LChS, .lccs and .csv files. See the requirements in the 'File Types' panel. Click on the green 'Load Legend' button to import the legend. Importing from the Land Cover Registry. From the menu toolbar select 'File' then 'Import' [Select 'Import' from the shortcut toolbar]. In the new 'Import Characterization Legend' window under 'Select Legend Source', select 'Land Cover Registry (LCLR)'. Wait for the registry to load and scroll through the list and select the legend you wish to import [Use the sort and filter buttons to rearrange the list as required]. Your browser does not support the video tag. Video: Importing a legend III. Export Legend Validate the legend. From the shortcut toolbar select 'Validate'. Review the messages in the notifications panel and address any issues with the legend to allow exporting. Exporting the legend. From the menu toolbar select 'File' then 'Export' [Select 'Export' from the shortcut toolbar]. (If 'Export' is greyed out, validate the legend and address any errors.) In the new 'Export Legend' panel select the export you require: Complete: Full export of the legend including LChS file, LCML XSD, legend diagram, class diagrams and CSV file in compressed ZIP file. LChS: Export of the legend as a LChS file. CSV: Export of the legend as a CSV file. Exporting the legend diagram. From the legend pane click 'Export diagram'. (If 'Export diagram' is inactive, validate the legend and address any errors.) Select the image format required: PNG, JPG or SVG. Exporting a class diagram. From the legend pane select the class' name tab to select the class you intend to export. From the legend pane click 'Export diagram'. (If 'Export diagram' is inactive, validate the legend and address any errors.) Select the image format required: PNG, JPG or SVG. Your browser does not support the video tag. Video: Exporting a legend Land Cover Semantic Interoperability Workflows I. Similarity Assessments From the menu toolbar select 'Resources' then 'Semantic Interoperability' then 'Similarity Assessment'. In the new 'Similarity Assessment' window under 'Compare legends for similarity by:', select 'Correspondence & Extensiveness' or 'Element Count' according to the comparison method preferred. Click on the blue 'Select Legends' button and navigate and select: - A reference legend file, against which other legends will be compared. (Ensure the reference legend file name includes the word 'Reference' for the system to identify it) - Legend files to be compared again the legend. (Hold Ctrl to select multiple files) [Drag and drop the reference legend and other legend files you wish to compare into the 'Drag and Drop Legend Files Here' area]. Note: LChS can process .LChS, .lccs and .csv files. See the requirements in the 'File Types' panel. Click on the green 'Process Legends' button to perform the similarity assessment. Click on the similarity value to see the calculation of the similarity. Click on 'Export (CSV)' to export the similarity results. Your browser does not support the video tag. Video: Similarity Assessment II. Legend Reassignment From the menu toolbar select 'Resources' then 'Semantic Interoperability' then 'Legend Connector'. In the new 'Select Reference Legend' choose a reference classification system to map your appointed legend against. Click 'Next' In 'Load Appointed' either - Select 'Upload File' to upload your appointed legend file to be mapped against the reference classification. Click 'Select Legend File' to select the appointed legend file [Drag and drop the appointed legend into the 'Drag and drop legend file here' area]. - Select 'Land Cover Registry (LCLR)' to select an appointed legend from the FAO Land Cover Registry to be mapped against the reference classification. Click on the 'Legend Name' or 'Actions' to select the appointed legend to import. Scroll down and click 'Next'. (Advanced users can adjust processing options in the window.) Scroll to the bottom of the window and click 'Start Processing'. Click 'View Results'. Click 'Export CSV', 'Export Excel' or 'Export JSON' to download the class reassignments that you can use in your GIS. To make adjustments or manually reassign classes: In the 'Matching Results' pane, select 'Log' to view the details of the class assignments From the 'Matching Details & Class Reassignment' pane click on the '+'. Scroll to the class you wish to reassign: Select 'Alternatives' to directly assign already computed alternatives. Select 'Reassign Class' pencil to select from all classes. Click 'Export CSV', 'Export Excel' or 'Export JSON' to download the class reassignments that you can use in your GIS. Your browser does not support the video tag. Video: Legend Reassignment
